title: Reduce dequant overhead with tiled-attention handoff and hybrid-precision prefetch
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: When using mixed-precision (INT8/FP8) serving paths the CPU/GPU boundary frequently pays a large tax in dequantization and re-encoding of KV cache slices during prefill and the early decode phase. For streaming/chat workloads with short prefix lengths this overhead is sometimes larger than the actual token decode cost, increasing tail-latency and per-token cost.

Objective: Implement a tiled-attention handoff and hybrid-precision prefetch strategy to: (1) minimize full dequant cycles by keeping most KV cache operations in packed INT8/FP8 formats, (2) enable zero-copy or on-GPU conversion for hot tiles, and (3) improve kernel selection heuristics so we route requests to the best precision path given sequence-length distribution and SLOs.

Scope: Design and implement new tiled-attention kernels (fusion-friendly, per-tile scaling), a lightweight handoff protocol between prefill and decode stages that preserves quantized tiles where safe, and a prefetch policy that materializes FP8 slices only for tiles predicted to be reaccessed during decode. This touches runtime kernel registry, prefill scheduler, and telemetry for per-tile miss/hot counters.
acceptance_criteria: P50 token latency for 16-64 prefix workloads on p4d decreases by >= 10% compared to current INT8 path baseline
End-to-end additional per-request CPU time for dequantization steps reduced by >= 40% for common chat prefix distributions
No regression (>5%) in perplexity or decoded token quality on regression prompt set
Kernel selector routes >= 85% of short-prefix (<64 tokens) requests to hybrid-precision-prefetch path when cost/lantency model predicts win
Automated bench harness and canary in staging validating both correctness and perf under mixed traffic
decisions: Prefer per-tile quantization scales vs per-head when tile reuse is high — reduces rematerialization cost
Implement a small on-GPU conversion ISP path for hot tiles (GPU-resident FP8 cache window) rather than CPU-side dequant for low-latency cases
Fallback policy: if tile reuse prediction confidence < 0.6, materialize in FP8 at decode-time to preserve numerical fidelity
Telemetry: emit per-request tile-hit/miss and quant-path chosen to runtime metrics with low-overhead sampling
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature-flagged kernel library and scheduler changes behind runtime flag 'tiled_prefetch_v1'. 2) Canary on dedicated internal workloads (10% of traffic) with perf and quality gating. 3) Expand to staging with mixed customer traffic and validation harness. 4) Gradual ramp to 100% with rollback window and automatic fallback to current INT8/FP8 path if SLOs break.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Numerical drift on edge prompts when keeping INT8 tiles longer. Mitigation: conservative QC checks and automatic quality regression alerts tied to prompt set evals.
Risk: Scheduler complexity increases latency P95. Mitigation: keep decision cost O(1) per request using cached heuristics; move heavy prediction to offline training and periodic refresh.
Risk: GPU memory spike from FP8 hot window. Mitigation: bounded hot-window size + eviction LRU policy and soft cap per-model.
Risk: Incompatibility with certain quantized kernel variants. Mitigation: implement clear capability flags in kernel registry and fallback to compatible kernels.
updates: 2025-03-01 - Created ticket and proposal. Initial microbenchmark shows 28% dequant CPU time reduction for single-stream chat on p3.utions.
2025-03-04 - Spike implementation: added tiled-attn prototype that performs per-tile scaling; observed 12% end-to-end latency win in synthetic workload.
2025-03-07 - Design review with infra and serving: agreed on on-GPU conversion path and telemetry events. Action: Diego to prototype GPU hot-window APIs.
2025-03-10 - Integrated tile-reuse predictor (simple LRU + recency score) into prefill scheduler; unit tests added for correctness. Submitting WIP PR #4219.

2025-03-12 - Canary plan drafted; QA to run regression suite. Need sign-off from ML quality leads before staging rollout. Noted two TODOs: tune per-tile scale quantization thresholds and add perf budget guardrails.
